exposure: interpregnancy interval groups (<24 months, 24-35 months, 36-59 months, >60 months)
outcome: success of vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC)
cohort: 36,653 pregnant women with one prior cesarean, who opted for trial of labor
finding: An interpregnancy interval of <24 months is not associated with a decreased success of vaginal birth after cesarean, while success rates decrease when the interval increases.
mod_finding: An interpregnancy interval of less than 24 months was not associated with decreased vaginal birth success after cesarean.
